Hilton adds three lifestyle properties in Thailand and Maldives to Apac portfolio
article:
Global hospitality firm Hilton announced three new lifestyle property signings across Asia Pacific (Apac), comprising a Curio Collection by Hilton hotel in Phuket, as well as two Tapestry Collection by Hilton properties in Chiang Mai and the Maldives.

The move is part of its broader strategy of doubling the luxury and lifestyle portfolio to meet rising demand for distinctive, experience-led stays in sought-after destinations.

Thailand will welcome two brand debuts. Andamanda Voyage, Curio Collection by Hilton, will mark the brand's first appearance in Phuket. Set within the city's Andamanda Waterpark complex in Kathu District, the resort is due to open by the end of the year.

The launch builds on Hilton's growing presence in the island, joining The Rawai Phuket — the company's first LXR Hotels & Resorts property, slated to open in 2027 as a nature-immersive retreat on Phuket's southern tip.

Further north, Hilton will bring its Tapestry Collection by Hilton brand to Chiang Mai for the first time. The 65-room property will be housed within a heritage building showcasing the artistry of Northern Thai architecture. It is situated in Old Town, a Unesco-recognised area in the city framed by ancient moats and temples.

In the Maldives, the company will unveil its first Tapestry Collection property, Coco de Mer Maldives, Tapestry Collection by Hilton. The 75-key resort, situated 25 minutes via speedboat from Velana International Airport, is set to open in June 2027. Alexandra Murray, vice president and regional head of Southeast Asia, says the signings “provide new opportunities to showcase our independent-spirited brands”.

They follow a string of upcoming Apac debuts. Canopy Bangkok Sukhumvit and Nivata Koh Samui, Tapestry Collection by Hilton are scheduled to open in August and October this year, respectively. More recently in July, Kahavadi Chiang Rai, Curio Collection by Hilton, opened its doors to guests as the first Hilton property in Northern Thailand.

title: German inflation accelerates to three-month high on energy bill
article:
(July 30): German inflation accelerated to the highest level in three months after temporary fuel-price relief expired and renewed fighting in the Middle East bolstered oil.

Consumer prices rose an annual 2.8% in July, the statistics office said on Thursday. That’s up from 2.4% in June and in line with the median estimate in a Bloomberg survey. Earlier, Spain reported a stronger-than-anticipated uptick to 3.8%

Data for France, Italy and the eurozone are due on Friday. Economists predict inflation in the latter edged up to 2.9%.

Reports on price pressures across the 21-nation eurozone in the first half of summer are a key input into the European Central Bank’s next decision on interest rates. Policymakers left borrowing costs unchanged last week, taking more time to analyse the implications of escalating attacks in and around Iran, while setting up September as an obvious moment for another hike.

Slovakia’s Governing Council member Peter Kazimir argued that at least one more step will be needed even if the situation improves, warning that officials mustn’t allow second-round effects to emerge. His Lithuanian counterpart Gediminas Simkus said the probability of a hike is “much higher” than that of a hold.

See also: Japan’s Takaichi calls for food sales tax cut to 1%, NHK says

Separate data earlier on Thursday showed Germany’s economy expanded more than expected in the second quarter, while numbers for the January-March period also saw an upward revision.

title: Yum reports strong Taco Bell sales in months before parasite-linked outbreak
article:
(July 30): Yum! Brands Inc’s Taco Bell business was booming before a parasite outbreak linked to tainted lettuce crimped sales.

The restaurant group said sales at established Taco Bell locations jumped 7% in the second quarter ended June 30, outpacing analyst estimates. The Mexican chain has been the fastest-growing brand in Yum’s portfolio, which also includes KFC and the soon-to-be-sold Pizza Hut business.

Thursday’s earnings report will likely be overshadowed by concerns about the outbreak that was discovered in the weeks since the quarter ended. In mid-July, US regulators tied Taco Bell lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms to the cyclospora parasite that has sickened thousands of people in Michigan and nearby states.

The company maintained its long-term financial targets, including 7% system sales growth excluding foreign currency fluctuations, but warned that the cyclospora outbreak could have an impact on future results.

Third-party data suggests Taco Bell traffic slumped upwards of 30% in the initial days after the company removed the affected lettuce, though specials such as US$1 Enchiritos have helped mitigate the impact since then.

Taco Bell had previously outpaced peers with an endless array of new offerings, including spicy nuggets and a jalapeño citrus salsa.

See also: US stocks fall as 30-year bond yields surge after Fed

“We are confident in the leadership of Taco Bell CEO Sean Tresvant and team to restore brand perceptions once broader publicity quiets down,” TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles wrote in a report ahead of the earnings release.

Second-quarter sales at KFC rose 2%, extending its growth streak, powered by demand in the Middle East, Latin America and Asia. Yum recently agreed to offload Pizza Hut, which has lost sales as it struggles to compete in a discount-driven category.

Yum shares dropped 1.4% at 7.13am in pre-market trading on Thursday. The stock has risen less than 1% so far this year as of Wednesday’s close, lagging a 6.9% increase in the S&P 500 Index.

title: Nscale to buy computing software firm Anyscale for US$1.65 bil
article:
(July 30): Cloud provider Nscale agreed to acquire software startup Anyscale to help customers use AI computing power more efficiently.

The deal price is about US$1.65 billion, according to a person familiar with the deal who asked not to be identified because the information is private.

San Francisco-based Anyscale offers software that helps artificial intelligence (AI) workloads run more effectively across separate servers and data centres. Bringing these capabilities within Nscale will allow customers to get quicker results and better performance, said Dan Bathurst, Nscale’s chief product officer.

“An engineer can now come to Nscale as a one-stop shop for all of their training, fine-tuning and inference services,” Bathurst said in an interview.

Formed from a cryptocurrency mining business in early 2024, London-based Nscale has quickly become one of the most prominent data centre newcomers riding the AI boom. The company leases AI-focused computing power and is developing massive data centres, including sites in Norway and West Virginia.

A number of these new computing providers, often called neoclouds, are working to differentiate themselves through software offerings. In May, rival Nebius Group NV said it would spend US$643 million to acquire Eigen AI, a startup focused on efficient delivery of AI models. “If you look at the other neoclouds, everyone’s wanting to move up the stack,” Bathurst said, meaning offering a wider range of services.

Anyscale said it generated 70% revenue growth in its most recent quarter compared with the previous period. All of the firm’s roughly 200 employees will join Nscale as part of the deal. Anyscale had raised funds in 2022 above a US$1 billion valuation.

Nscale said last year that it plans to IPO, potentially as soon as the second half of 2026. Its board includes former Meta Platforms Inc executives Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg.

title: Pakistan strikes deal with Iran for safe passage of LNG shipment — Bloomberg
article:
(July 30): Pakistan has negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for at least one Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipment, according to people with knowledge of the matter, the latest effort by the South Asian nation to use its diplomatic ties to ease a deepening energy crunch.

The Al Areesh — which had been idling in the Persian Gulf since loading cargo at Qatar’s Ras Laffan export terminal in early July — transited the Strait of Hormuz early on Thursday, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. The ship crossed with its transponders switched on and is now signalling Pakistan as its destination.

The deal to secure the safe crossing could cover other cargoes, one of the people added.

Pakistan, which has suffered acute fuel shortages since the start of the war, has leveraged its diplomatic channels to act as an intermediary in talks between the US and Iran. Earlier in the year it used those ties to negotiate with Tehran for the safe passage of several LNG cargoes.

However, the latest flare-up in violence — along with an Iranian attack on a Qatari LNG tanker — effectively halted deliveries to Pakistan. The South Asian nation relies heavily on Qatar for the fuel, and cancelled deliveries has resulted in rolling blackouts in parts of the the country.

Pakistan’s petroleum ministry didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Qatar’s International Media Office and Iran’s foreign ministry also did not immediately respond to Bloomberg queries.

See also: Oil holds gain as Trump vows to hit Iran and US stockpiles slump

It is not clear whether any payment was made to guarantee the crossing.

Since the war began in late-February, Pakistan has been forced to pay over US$400 million (RM1.63 billion) to procure LNG shipments from spot markets to replace supplies from Qatari, its top producers, according to Bloomberg calculations.

title: Blue Owl’s Stack seeking US$5.9 bil loan, extending AI debt boom — Bloomberg
article:
(July 30): Blue Owl Capital’s data centre firm Stack Infrastructure Inc is seeking an A$8.5 billion (US$5.9 billion) syndicated loan to fund its latest project in Melbourne, according to people familiar with the matter, in what could be one of the largest such financings to the sector in Australia.

Proceeds raised will back Stack Infrastructure’s third data centre in Melbourne, the people said, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters. Talks with banks are still at an early stage and the details may change, they added.

A representative for both Blue Owl and Stack Infrastructure declined to comment.

Australia is emerging as one of the most attractive markets in the Asia-Pacific for data centres, in part due to its massive land area, as well as abundant renewable energy resources, a stable political environment and strong connectivity to the region through low-latency submarine cables. The sector’s investment pipeline is expected to exceed A$155 billion, equivalent to 5.6% of Australia’s annual gross domestic product, according to Westpac Banking Corp.

Beyond mounting concerns about the billions of dollars being raised to fund the data centre boom, Australia is also among a growing number of countries seeking to regulate artificial intelligence (AI) without stifling innovation. The government is looking to impose environmental and energy controls on the country’s data centre investment pipeline, which Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has said would be the first in the world.

Stack Infrastructure’s latest borrowing comes on the heels of another multibillion loan for Blackstone’s AirTrunk Pty in Sydney. Separately, the company is also mulling a sale of assets in Australia, Japan and Malaysia that could be valued at more than US$30 billion.

See also: Meta’s Zuckerberg defends AI bets to skeptical investors

Stack Infrastructure operates data centres in cities across the Americas, Europe and Asia, including Sydney and Melbourne in Australia, according to its website. Alternative asset manager Blue Owl acquired the operator as part of its takeover of IPI Partners LLC last year.

title: Hongkong Land's SCPREF makes maiden acquisition with $1.1 bil Wheelock Place deal
article:
Hongkong Land Holdings, via its Singapore Central Private Real Estate Fund, plans to acquire Wheelock Place for $1.1 billion from Wharf Real Estate Investment Company, in line with valuation.

This marks the fund's first acquisition, excluding the seed properties that consists of a one third stake in MBFC Towers 1 and 2, one third stake in One Raffles Quay and Asia Square Tower 1.

Upon planned completion by the end August, SCPREF’s AUM will increase to $9.4 billion from S$8.2 billion at inception – a significant step towards its target AUM of $15 billion.

Hongkong Land says this deal is aligned with its strategy of growing recurring earnings and expanding its fund management platform. In an interview in May, group CFO Craig Beattie had said SCPREF had a specific focus. It's Singapore-only, and the assets must be located in Marina Bay for office and on Orchard Road for retail.

SCPREF, with Hongkong Land as the manager and single largest unitholder, was established to pursue growth opportunities in Singapore’s commercial real estate market through high-quality acquisitions and to drive value through active asset management, operational enhancements and long-term value creation.

Wheelock Place consists of a 21-storey commercial building and two basement levels incorporating offices, shopping podium and car parks, with a total gross floor area of approximately 43,280 sqm.

See also: Pasir Panjang Road freehold site for sale at $70 mil

Its prime location, established office and retail offering, and long-term growth potential make it a highly strategic addition to SCPREF’s portfolio, says Hongkong Land.

The acquisition also supports the Fund’s investment mandate of acquiring high-quality, income-generating commercial assets in Singapore’s Central Business District and the Orchard Road precinct, says Hongkong Land.

"SCPREF was created to acquire assets of a calibre that rarely come to market, and Wheelock Place is precisely that," says Hongkong Land CEO Michael T Smith.

See also: JTC launches design and build tender for first of two blocks in Kampong AI

"To have secured this premium asset within months of the Fund's launch reflects both the effectiveness of our fund management team and the confidence of our capital partners," he adds.
